newsitem.title: ITALY: France asked to help Italy's Airbus bid - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: France asked to help Italy's Airbus bid - Prodi.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he had asked France to help Italy's bid to join the Airbus consortium.

French-based Airbus Industrie consortium is trying to bring other European aircraft makers into its plans to transform its four-nation industry and state cooperative structure into an autonomous corporation.
The consortium is currently made up of German, British, French and Spanish companies.
"Over industrial co-operation there are absolutely no problems," Prodi told a news conference following a summit meeting with French President Jacques Chirac in this southern port city.
"We have prepared ways for working together in the aerospace and telecommunications sectors. French support for Italy's entry into the Airbus consortium is important," he added.
Manfred Bischoff, head of Airbus member company Daimler Aerospace, said in August that the consortium wanted to see Italy's Alenia, a unit of state-controlled Finmeccanica, join the consortium.
